claims.statement: For a finite birth-death CTMC on 0..M with death rate gamma*n and state birth cap B, a probability vector pi is stationary-realizable iff it is normalized, nonnegative, and gamma*(n+1)*pi[n+1] <= B*pi[n] for every n<M; the average birth intensity then equals gamma*E[N].
claims.novelty_boundary: General occupation-measure LP prior art is established; the one-dimensional slope form is a direct specialization.
costs: observation and actuation costs omitted by model
claims.falsifier: A normalized pi satisfying all slope constraints but not realizable, or a realizable stationary law violating one of the constraints.
claims.next_gate: If an implementation costed controller is required, add observation bandwidth and rate-switching cost to the state-action LP.

claims.statement: At M=2, B=gamma=1, h=2, and mean 1/2, a single-cutoff rate policy is strictly suboptimal for minimizing P(N<h): cutoff dropout is 1, while rates (2/5,1) attain dropout 7/8.
assumptions: single-cutoff means full rate below cutoff, zero above, with optional fractional rate only at the cutoff
claims.proof_path: CYCLE2_REPORT.md, Exact failure of a single-cutoff rate rule
claims.novelty_boundary: A finite example only; it rejects universal cutoff optimality for this criterion, not threshold results under other costs.
costs: state-dependent observation and rate adjustment are assumed free
claims.falsifier: Recompute either stationary law and show the mean/dropout pair is incorrect.
claims.next_gate: Use as a unit test for any proposed numerical or analytic cutoff theorem.

claims.statement: For two unit-capacity queues, equal deaths gamma, equal fixed means m, and target exact joint mass p=P(N1=N2=1), the least pointwise shared birth cap is gamma*max(p/(m-p), 2*(m-p)/(1-2*m+p)); the displayed feedback policy attains it whenever the four stationary masses are positive.
claims.status: exact internal derivation with reversible realizing policy
claims.proof_path: CYCLE2_REPORT.md, Shared cap: exact two-output theorem
claims.novelty_boundary: Finite two-output specialization and exact formula; general CTMDP LP methods are prior art.
costs: statewise peak observation intensity given in report
claims.falsifier: A stationary policy meeting the same m,p under a cap below the formula, or failure of the reversible construction to realize the specified masses.
claims.next_gate: Add bounded observation/switching costs or derive a scalable structural policy for K outputs.

claims.statement: For two outputs of capacity one with gamma=1, means 1/2 each, the maximum joint success at cap B is B/(2*(B+1)) for B>=sqrt(2), and the means are infeasible for B<sqrt(2). For exact success p in (0,1/2), B_exact(p)=max(2p/(1-2p),(1-2p)/p); for at-least-p success B_atleast(p)=max(sqrt(2),2p/(1-2p)).
assumptions: perfect state observation and zero delay
claims.novelty_boundary: No general K-output formula for an efficient index policy is established.
claims.falsifier: Direct balance-equation violation or a feasible policy outside the stated exact cap interval.
claims.next_gate: Study finite sensing frequency and switching penalties before claiming a deployable controller.
